newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Citizen to make watches in India.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Citizen to make watches in India.

text.p: Japan's leading watch maker Citizen Watch Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it would produce and sell watches in India from next year to target the growing middle class there.

"We decided to begin production in India as the government is lifting restrictions and abandoning protectionist policies. Also, a middle-class population is growing as well," a company spokesman said.
Citizen hopes to begin producing middle- and higher-priced watches at the venture, Citizen Watches (India) Co Ltd, in Madras from next April, the spokesman said.
The venture will be 25.5 percent owned by Citizen Watch, 25.5 percent by Citizen Trading Co, a Citizen Watch unit, and 49 percent by Doshi Times Industries Ltd of India, Citizen said in a statement.
Capitalisation will be about 240 million yen ($2.1 million), it said.
The venture hopes to produce 200,000 units in the first year of operation, rising to 500,000 units in the second year and one million in the third year, Citizen Watch said.
Initially, the venture will assemble imported parts and components, but hopes to increase local purchases in the future, the spokesman said.
But the watch movements will continue to be imported from Japan.
Citizen has said it would not shift production of the movements, a core component of a watch, overseas.
"We will keep production of the movements in Japan as it is the key part of our business," the spokesman said.
The Indian venture is Citizen's fifth tie-up in Asia. It already has ventures in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and South Korea, the spokesman said. ($1=114)
